Subject: Internal: evidence checklist and proposed DPA language for Medicloud

Team —

Draft checklist for the external pack (ops_evidence_matrix.xlsx attached to this thread):
- Written assurance (signed) that customer traffic will not be used for model training or research (no-train), including how variants/backup models are handled.
- Snapshot of retention configuration: request logs (30 days), full interaction store (90 days default; can be reduced to 30 on request), ephemeral KV cache TTLs (max 300s for prompt-response caching unless explicitly configured otherwise).
- KMS key residency: proof that KEKs for Medicloud keys are provisioned in US regions; HSM-backed key IDs and permissible export operations documented.
- Export controls: list of subprocessors with onshore processing guarantees and transfer controls.
- Latency impact table for routing to dedicated/onshore pool (estimated p50/p90/p99 deltas).
- Audit traces: sample anonymized trace showing no model update pipeline triggered.

Proposed DPA snippet for prompt/response custody (subject to legal review):
"Redwood will not use Customer Data, including prompts and model responses, to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any models or datasets used in Redwood's services without Customer's prior written consent. Customer Data processed by Redwood will be stored, processed, and deleted in accordance with the retention settings agreed in Appendix A; derivative or aggregated telemetry will not contain Customer-identifiable prompts or responses"

I'll take initial redline of their PDF once Laura confirms operational values.

David
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Team —

Operational notes to include in the pack (I will export into ops_evidence_matrix.xlsx):
- Retention: interaction store purge job runs nightly; default tenant window is 90 days but for Medicloud we can set 30 days on request and provide proof of purge via job logs.
- KV/prefix cache: TTLs default at 120s; configurable at route level up to 300s. We can annotate which endpoints will have KV disabled.
- Logs and traces: we can provide an anonymized sample trace covering request path, model variant used, and routing decision (no payload) to show no training pipeline hooks.
- Subprocessors: current list attached; for Medicloud we will ensure any transfer to a third-party inference cache is onshore or blocked.
- KMS: we can allocate a customer-managed KEK in us-west-2 with HSM protection; export of key material is not permitted.
- SLA exception: routing to dedicated onshore pool will be via a policy that pins to nodes in the dedicated region. Expected impact: +25ms p50, +80ms p99 on average for the affected endpoints; throughput commitments remain the same but host utilization will be higher.

I attached a first-pass redline of their DPA with the proposed prompt/response custody clause embedded (Medicloud_DPA_Redline_20261212.pdf). Please review and advise if Legal wants stronger wording on derivatives/aggregates.

Laura
